en: Hi, this is Spendline, for the FuriosaAI and Bricksum track, challenge B. Our claim is simple. Not an agent that can pay, but a payment that can prove it was allowed. A person grants a budget, a seller list and a deadline. The agent, on Kiln, proposes purchases. A vault on TRON pays only inside that line, and records every stop.

Picture a 3-person AI startup. The lead hands the weekly GPU and inference budget to a purchasing agent. Then a teammate asks: why did we buy this? Payment rails say who paid whom, not who allowed it. The lead needs one receipt that answers, and someone else must be able to check it without trusting anyone.

Here is the split. Kiln reads the request words and returns a small JSON. Code picks the offer and does the money math. The vault enforces the line. And anyone can audit the result with no key. The model phrases, the audit decides.

Boundaries are enforced on-chain, in the vault's pay function. We recorded 4 stops on TRON Nile: a seller not on the list, over budget once fees are added, a payment after the person pressed STOP, and one after the time window closed. A replayed receipt hash was stopped too. Each stop is an event with its reason, never a silent revert.

Kiln does real work, and we count it. The request is read through a Kiln tool call, chosen over plain JSON by a rule we fixed before a live test. 1.00 LLM call per purchase, against a design limit of 2. 26 live Kiln calls across 3 flows, 18,490 tokens in total. No-think cut median output from 223 to 36 tokens, with the same JSON. Energy is an estimate we state: 180 watts times measured time.

On the chain, the agent reads the line, writes pay with the receipt hash, and the vault settles test USDT to the seller. Every receipt hash appears in exactly one Paid or SpendBlocked event. The person signs grant and STOP with the owner key, on their own machine.

Approval and evidence. One command, no key, rebuilds every verdict from the receipts file and the vault's public events: 8 receipts, 4 paid inside, 4 stopped, 0 problems, 13.60 USDT paid. Edit a receipt and the hash chain breaks. Drop one and the vault event with no receipt is flagged.

What is new: a stop is an event, so the history shows what the agent was not allowed to do. Receipts are hash-chained and anchored in the vault. And the model's explanations are shown only when they repeat the audit and use numbers from the record.

Where it plugs in: wherever an agent would call a wallet, it calls the vault instead. We measured what one guarded decision costs on Nile: 8.51 TRX when paid, 2.80 when stopped, plus a fraction of a cent of Kiln. Who needs it: teams that let agents buy compute and credits. Our business hypothesis, not yet validated: open vault and audit, with a hosted audit and alerts as the paid layer.

What is not done, stated: testnet only, as the brief asks. One line per vault. Signing is on the person's machine, not in the browser. Energy is an estimate. And parts were built before the event window; the README lists every commit.
Please check it yourself: install, run the audit, and open the UI. Spendline. A payment that can prove it was allowed. Thank you.
